questions.question: When was the first Home Rule League started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The first Home Rule League was started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in **1916**__.
 
• The objective of the movement was to establish self government.
 
• He founded it in Belgaum at the Bombay provincial congress.
 
• Later , it was launched by Annie Besant in September 1916.

questions.question: Captain Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe visited India during the reign of _________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Captain Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe visited India during the reign of Mughal Emperor **Jahangir**__.
 
• Jahangir was the 4th Emperor of the Mughal dynasty.
 
• Captain Hawkins represented the English East India Company and travelled to Agra in 1609 to meet Jahangir.
 
• Sir Thomas Roe met him in the year 1615.
 
• He arrived as the ambassador from King James I of England.

questions.question: Nirmala Sitharaman announced that National Sports Education Board for development of sportspersons to be set up under ________ while presenting the Budget of 2019.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Nirmala Sitharaman announced that National Sports Education Board for development of sportspersons to be set up under **Khelo India**__ while presenting the Budget of 2019.
 
• Khelo India is the initiative of the Indian government.

questions.question: Who built the magnificent cave temples 'Ratha' in Mahabalipuram?
questions.solution:
__
 
• King **Narsimha**__ built the magnificent cave temples 'Ratha' in Mahabalipuram.
 
• The temple was built in the 7th and 8th century.
 
• The temple town of Mahabalipuram is situated along the shores of Bay of Bengal.
 
• It is known for its mandapas, rathas, and the temple of Rivage.
 
• There are a total of 8 rathas situated in Mahabalipuram.
 
• Out of these, 1 is named after Draupadi and 5 are named after Pandavas.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT an example of Bryophyta?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Chara**__ is not a bryophyte.
 
• It is a green algae which is found in lakes and freshwater ponds.
 
• Bryophytes are a group of plant species which reproduce through spores instead of seeds or flowers.
 
• Marchantia and Funaria are crytogamae while Riccia are liverworts.
 
• Bryophytes are relatively small compared to the seed-bearing plants.

questions.question: What is the real name of Sister Nivedita?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The real name of Sister Nivedita is **Margaret Elizabeth Noble**__.
 
• She was a follower of Swami Vivekananda.
 
• It was him who gave her the name Nivedita.
 
• She was an Anglo-Irish social worker.
 
• In 1898, she established a school for girls, who were deprived of basic education.

questions.question: When was the Citizenship Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1955.**__

__
 
• The Citizenship Act was passed in the year **1955**__.
 
• According to it, the President of India is the first citizen of India.
 
• The Act was amended several times by the amendment acts in the years 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, and 2019.
 
• Part II of the Indian Constitution deals with citizenship.
 
• It is covered under articles 5-11.

questions.question: Laterite soil is rich in Iron and ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Laterite soils are rich in oxides of** iron and aluminum**__ but deficient in nitrogen and potash.
 
• As it is poor in nitrogen, it is not fertile and poor for agriculture
 
• It is majorly found in higher areas of Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It is found as a result of decomposition due to heavy rainfall and high temperature.

questions.question: A Golden Slam is winning ________ Grand Slam tournaments as well as the Olympics Gold Medal.
questions.solution:
__
 
• A Golden Slam is winning **4**__ Grand Slam tournaments as well as the Olympics Gold Medal.
 
• If a team or player wins all the 4 consecutively, but not in the same calendar year, then that is known as Non-Calendar Year Grand Slam.
 
• The 4 Grand Slam tournaments are US Open, Wimbledon, French Open, and Australian Open.
 
• The term Golden Slam was created in the year 1988 when Steffi Graf won gold medal in tennis at the Summer Olympics and all 4 Grand Slam tournaments.
 
• In tennis, it is one of the rarest achievements.

questions.question: When was the Environment Protection Act passed?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Environment Protection Act was passed in the year **1986**__.
 
• The main objective was to provide improvement and protection of environment and matters concerned with it.
 
• The Act was enacted in the wake of the Bhopal Tragedy by the Government of India.
 
• It is covered under Article 253 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: How many articles were there in the original Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• There were **395**__ articles in the Constitution of India originally.
 
• It also had 8 schedules and 22 parts.
 
• __**Now, it consists of 448 articles in 12 schedules and 25 parts.**__
 
• So far, 104 amendments have been made to the Constitution so far.
 
• The Constitution officially came into force on 26 January 1950.

__**Please note we have asked , initially , meaning when the constitution came to effect on 25 jan 1950.**__

questions.question: ________ is considered as the oldest discovered Indus Valley Civilization site.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhirrana.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhirrana**__ is considered the oldest discovered Indus Valley Civilization site.
 
• It is the oldest one according to the C-14 radio-dating done by the Archaeological Survey of India.
 
• It is situated in the Fatehabad district and dates to 757-6200 BC.
 
• Rakhigarhi, situated close to Bhirrama is the largest Harappan site in the world.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro is situated in southern Pakistan.
 
• Allahdino is located towards each of Karachi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was spread from present-day North-East Afghanistan to Pakistan and North-West India. This civilization flourished in the river basins of the Ghaggar-Hakra river and the Indus. Indus valley civilization is one of the four oldest civilizations in the world. It is also known as Harappan Civilization and is well-known for its organized planning based on the grid system. Important facts to be remembered 
 
• John Marshall was the first researcher to use the term, ‘Indus Valley Civilization’.
 
• Indus Valley Civilization spread from the year 2500 – 1750 BC according to radio-carbon dating.
 
• The most distinctive feature of the Harappan Civilization was its urbanization.
 
• Moreover, sheep and goats, dogs, humped cattle buffalo, and elephants were domesticated in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• The capital cities are Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
 
• The port cities are Sutkagendor, Balakot, Lothal, Allahdino, and Kuntasi.
 
• The Indus valley people were well-acquainted with the use of both cotton and wool.
 
• Name of the major cities are given below:
 
 
• Mohenjodaro (Sind)-It is located on the right bank of the Indus.
 
• Kalibangan (Rajasthan)-It was on the banks of the river Ghaggar river
 
• Chanhudaro-It lies on the left bank of the Indus in the south of Mohenjodaro.
 
• Lothal- It is located at the head of the Gulf of Cambay.
 
• Surkotada (Gujarat)-It is at the head of the Rann of Kutch.
 
• Banawali (Haryana)-It was situated on the banks of the now-extinct Sarasvati
 
• Dholavira (Gujarat)-It excavated is in the Kutch district

questions.question: Car moving on a straight road is an example of ________ motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rectilinear**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

__
 
• Car moving on a straight road is an example of **rectilinear**__ motion.
 
• When two particles of a body travel same distance along 2 parallel straight lines then that is known as Rectilinear motion or straight-line motion.
 
• Periodic motion is that which is repeated in equal intervals of time.
 
• Curvilinear motion is that which occurs when a particle travels along a curved path.
 
• Random motion is an unpredictable motion in which the object moves in a random direction.
